title: Halloween
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; Word File German translations suggested separately

entries.example: What's your favourite Halloween tradition?
entries.description: Something people do every year for a long time, like at Christmas

entries.example: We do not fear the zombies.
entries.description: To be afraid of something

entries.example: We cut off the top of the pumpkin.
entries.description: To take away a part with a knife or scissors

entries.example: We put some vampire stickers on his front window.
entries.description: The glass in the wall of a house that faces the street

entries.example: Let's keep the pumpkin for our Halloween party.
entries.description: To not give something away

entries.example: I was very proud.
entries.description: To feel very happy about something good you or others did

entries.example: We walk up the stairs in the dark.
entries.description: You walk up these to get to the next floor

entries.example: I put a vampire sticker on his window.
entries.description: A small picture you can put on things

entries.example: Children get sweets for Halloween.
entries.description: Things like chocolate and candy

entries.example: We knock on people's doors and say "Trick or treat!".
entries.description: Children say this at the door on Halloween night

entries.example: I need a knife to cut vegetables.
entries.description: You use it to cut food

entries.example: She was dressed like a girl from the 19th century.
entries.description: 100 years

entries.example: Her costume looks great. She looks like a real vampire.
entries.description: Special clothes you wear to look like someone else

entries.example: Laura couldn't stop.
entries.description: Was not able to: I ___ sleep last night.

entries.example: Look at my cat. Isn't it cute?
entries.description: Small and sweet, like a baby animal

entries.example: The dress is beautiful. You can wear it to the party.
entries.description: A piece of clothing for girls and women, with a skirt

entries.example: The house is next to the graveyard.
entries.description: A place where dead people are buried

entries.example: I often talk to myself.
entries.description: I like ___. I am a nice person.

entries.example: Where shall we go?
entries.description: ___ we go to the cinema tonight?

entries.example: I feel a bit sick. I ate too many sweets.
entries.description: How you feel when your stomach hurts or you are ill

entries.example: She was dressed up as her favourite superheroine.
entries.description: A woman or girl with special powers who helps people

entries.example: You shouldn't play any wild games.
entries.description: Not calm, very fast and noisy

entries.example: At Halloween, some costumes really scare me.
entries.description: To make someone afraid

entries.example: You should always wear a cycle helmet.
entries.description: You wear it on your head when you ride a bike

entries.example: Come on, guys. Don't look. Promise.
entries.description: A friendly word for a group of people: Hi ___, how are you?

entries.example: I don't want to lose my phone.
entries.description: To not find something anymore, or to not win

entries.example: Let's have a picnic in the park.
entries.description: A meal you eat outside, for example in a park
A big orange vegetable; people cut faces into it for Halloween
A scary person in stories who drinks blood
A woman in stories who does magic and flies on a broom
The spirit of a dead person; it can go through walls
A Halloween game: you try to get fruit out of water with your mouth
You wear it over your face so people can't see who you are
